newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa has brushed aside a spectre of abandonment by his political allies and declared himself ready to face the opposition's censure assault that begins in parliament today. (BANGKOK POST)

- Outgoing armed forces chiefs and their successors led by Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh called on Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa. The new appointees, announced on Tuesday, pledged they would refrain from playing politics. Several close aides to Chavalit were promoted to key slots in the Army. (THE NATION)
- The Board of Trade, Thailand's largest business association, issues strong recommendation asking Prime Minister Banharn to resign. (THE NATION)

- Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan has denied news reports that Bangkok Bank of Commerce scandal suspect Rakesh Saxena could have also financially contributed to Amnuay's Nam Thai Party. He said the allegation was groundless and said he will sue Saxena if he actually levelled a charge. (THE NATION)
- The Cabinet has approved the appointment of Krirk-krai Jirapaet, director general of the Business Economics Department, as Thailand's new Ambassador to the World Trade Organisation. (BANGKOK POST)

- Academicians have critised plans drafted by the government-run National Economic and Social Development Board on Thailand's economic cooperation with its neighbouring countries. They say that the plans would be difficult to implement because Thailand would gain more than the others. (MANAGER)
- Japanese electronics company NEC Technologies (Thailand) will open an 828 million baht tantalum chip capacitor and temperature fuse factory today. (BUSINESS DAY)
- Government to consider lifting quota on livestock feed raw materials. (BUSINESS DAY)
